findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Every item with a priority record is kept, even past the cap, so the request's 'set most recently by a person first' ranking is never used, and the case that prompted the request (13 urgent items set by hand) would not shrink.
findings.evidence: Store.rs:89-99: Job::priority() uses the latest priority record first, so items re-tiered by hand with `athena priority` all count as person-set. The request says 'keeping the ones set most recently by a person first', which only makes sense if some person-set items can be demoted. The accepted reading says they are never demoted below their own record. The plan follows the reading and raises the conflict as an open question. Fix: Keep the open question, and say it plainly in the CHANGELOG and help text: if all 13 urgent items have priority records, the cap demotes none of them. Within the kept person-set group, order by the latest priority record's `at` (most recent first), so the ranking exists if the owner later lets the cap bind them.

findings.summary: drain.rs is outside the listed deliverables. The plan explains why it is needed, and the code supports that.
findings.evidence: Drain.rs:2008 is the only production call to Plan::build_with, and Steps (drain.rs:507) already has defaulted methods such as job_history and plan_entry, so a defaulted priority_caps fits that pattern. Athena flagged the scope as well. Fix: Keep the change. In the summary, name drain.rs as a required extra file and give the reason.

findings.summary: When loading config or records fails, the plan quietly falls back to no caps.
findings.evidence: Step 8: 'on error return no caps'. If athena.toml is malformed, the caps would be skipped without any notice. Fix: Print a note (for example through self.note_once) when the caps cannot be loaded, so a missing cap is visible.

summary: This round-3 plan holds up against the code. Plan::build_with is called in production only at drain.rs:2008 (Drain::prepare). Steps (drain.rs:507) already uses defaulted methods, so a defaulted priority_caps keeps the fake test impls compiling. RealSteps already calls JobConfig::at (drain.rs:3217). effective_priorities and priority_violations (plan.rs:465-514) work as the plan describes. Job::priority() (store.rs:92) applies the latest priority record first, so the plan's 'own priority' is entry.priority, as it claims. The Intervention path pattern (records.rs:2826) is a sound model for records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, and PriorityRecord's n counter is a sound model for ordering focus records. commit_records_to exists at tests/drain.rs:4605. The redesign caps each item's own priority, then reruns the existing raising logic. That fixes the earlier problem where raised prerequisites could push out the urgent item that raised them, and it keeps priority_violations consistent with the plan. Each demonstration names a real seam: build_capped unit tests, a drain.rs Stub test, and the real binary on a Fixture with records written into it. Each would fail without the behavior, and the binary test first asserts that all 5 items are planned, which guards against incomplete entries. What remains is minor. The person-set rule follows the accepted reading but means the motivating case of 13 urgent items set by hand would not shrink; the plan flags this as an open question. Athena already flagged that drain.rs is outside the deliverables, and the plan justifies it. The silent fallback to no caps on error is a nit.
